newsitem.title: JAPAN: No sign Russia selling PGMs in spot market-traders.
newsitem.headline: No sign Russia selling PGMs in spot market-traders.

text.p: There have not been any signs that Russia has resumed sales of platinum group metals (PGMs) in the spot market, Japanese traders said on Friday.
They said prices of the platinum group metals could rise if the suspension were to continue into the middle of next week.

Several trade houses hoped to buy palladium in the spot market in June for their immediate requirements, while others were keenly waiting for Russian PGM supplies under long-term contracts to arrive in Japan at around July 10-15, they said.
The Japanese have signed contracts for July-December deliveries with Russia's platinum group metals agency Almaz.

"I think some trade houses were expecting Russia to sell the metals in the spot market in late June. The Japanese palladium market will be hurt severely if Russia fails to resume exports in June," one precious metal industry source said.
Supply problems in the Japanese palladium market have been quite serious since Russia suspended PGM exports more than five months ago, they said.
"I asked one trade house if there are any available metals for us to buy, but the trade house said it has only metals that are almost like scrap," the source said.
Several traders said, however, they were advised by Russia's platinum group metals agency Almaz that it had been granted an export licence.
"I think its only a matter of paperwork before Russia resumes PGM exports," he said.
Some Japanese traders said they thought the protracted suspension of PGM exports was partly due to the possible change in Russia's PGM marketing policy to one of keeping PGM prices high.
Late last year, Russia sold palladium at low prices, pushing palladium prices sharply down.
Palladium prices have doubled since the suspension.
Japan is the world largest consumer of platinum group metals. Russia supplies more than 60 percent of world palladium and 20 percent of platinum.
